Hi John / Amy — following up with the benchmark results I mentioned. See attached PDF and CSV for raw numbers. Quick summary below.

Summary (test config):
- Model: open-llama-13b-qlora-equivalent
- Request payload: average 200 tokens (prompt) + generation up to 256 tokens
- Hardware: Redwood Hosted (multi-tenant NVIDIA A10) vs Redwood Dedicated (reserved A100 pod)

Results (median / p95):
- Hosted (A10 / shared): p50 = 62 ms, p95 = 185 ms, sustained throughput ~65 req/sec (continuous batching enabled)
- Dedicated (A100 pod): p50 = 28 ms, p95 = 98 ms, sustained throughput ~220 req/sec (larger batch windows + optimized kernels)

Notes:
- p95 in hosted is borderline for your 200ms SLA at the tail with continuous bursts — prefix caching and tighter batching configs can improve tail latency by ~10-15%.
- Dedicated capacity gives comfortable headroom for your 500 qps peak if sharded across 2-3 pods with autoscale; cost will be higher but predictable.
- Attached CSV contains per-run samples and the exact kernel/sequence config used.

Attachments: acme_latency_benchmarks_v1.pdf (summary), acme_kpi_sample_results.csv (raw samples)

If useful I can carve out 30 minutes next week to walk through the CSV and show the trace slices that explain the tail behavior.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Systems Engineer, Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
